rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibrahim's request that the town be safe asks that his own heart be secured from separation and veiling.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أراد بهذا أن يجعل

rows.speaker: السياري
rows.claim: The idols from which Ibrahim asks protection are the passions one follows.
rows.anchor: قال السياري : أن تعبد الأهواء

rows.speaker: الدينوري
rows.claim: People's idols take many forms: the self, children, wealth, trade, spouse, or one's spiritual state; each person is bound to one.
rows.anchor: قال الدينوري : الأصنام مختلفة فمنهم من صنمه نفسه ، ومنهم من صنمه ولده

rows.speaker: الدينوري
rows.claim: Disavowing these idols means claiming no spiritual state or impossibility for oneself, relying on no deed, and returning blame for every good or evil to oneself without self-satisfaction.
rows.anchor: كل واحد من الخلق مربوط بصنم من هذه الأصنام ، والتبرىء أي من هذه الأصنام

rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: Ja'far reads the prayer as asking not to be returned to witnessing Abraham's intimate friendship with God, nor his children to witnessing prophethood.
rows.anchor: قال جعفر : لا تردني إلى مشاهدة الخلة ولا ترد أولادي

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: After God ordered Abraham to build the Kaaba, He rebuked him for asking acceptance as though the building were his favor; Abraham had forgotten God's benefaction and foregrounded his own deed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : إن الله تعالى أمر إبراهيم ببناء الكعبة

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: The self is the worst idol when it follows desire and its own interests; Abraham asks that God occupy the self and cut it off from all besides Him.
rows.anchor: قال : واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام أي نفسي شر صنم

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: The idols of intimacy and reliance are intrusive thoughts of heedlessness and fleeting moments of attachment.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أن تعبد أصنام الخلة والركون إليها وهو خطرات

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Every self has an idol of desire, except the self purified through divine enabling.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا : أن تعبد الأنفس لأن لكل نفس صنما من الهوى

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd reads the prayer as asking to be prevented from drawing near to God through anything besides God.
rows.anchor: قال الجنيد : واجنبني وبني ، أي امنعني

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Abraham did not curse those who disobeyed him; he named God's forgiveness and mercy, acknowledging that he had no claim over God's servants.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : لما هرب الخليل في استرزاقه للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Settling his descendants means placing them in God's presence by taking them beyond the bounds of known things and formal conventions.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أسكنتهم حضرتك بإخراجي إياهم عن حدود

rows.speaker: آخر
rows.claim: Another says God eased their return to Him by allowing nothing in the two worlds to distract them from Him.
rows.anchor: قال آخر : سهلت عليهم طريق الرجوع إليك ليلا بمجرهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Their dwelling in the barren valley taught them reliance on God and abandonment of reliance on material causes.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : علمتهم بذلك طريق التوكل وترك الاعتماد

words: فَٱجْعَلْ أَفْـِٔدَةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهْوِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ
rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: Ja'far explains that people's hearts incline toward Abraham's family because their own hearts incline toward God.
rows.anchor: قال جعفر : لأن أفئدتهم تهوي إليك

words: فَٱجْعَلْ أَفْـِٔدَةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهْوِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ
rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: When someone withdraws completely from creation, God turns people's faces toward him and places affection for him in their hearts; Abraham prayed this for his family after cutting them off from people, provision, and causes.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : من انقطع عن الخلق بالكلية صرف الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الخواص
rows.claim: Al-Khawwas reads what Abraham hides as love of God and what he declares as remembrance of Him.
rows.anchor: قال الخواص : ما نخفي من حبك وما نعلن

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata reads the hidden as spiritual states and the manifest as proper devotional conduct.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ما نخفي من الأحوال

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان
rows.claim: Abu Uthman urges purifying the secret, cultivating the inner self, and correcting hidden affairs, since nothing is hidden from God.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : طهر سرك وأعمر باطنك وأصلح خفيات

words: وَمَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍۢ
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: God alone originates what is absent and brings hidden realities of accord and opposition into view.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : تفرد الحق بإيجاد المفقودات

rows.speaker: الحسين
rows.claim: Al-Husayn reads what is hidden as companionship with God and what is declared as ecstatic love.
rows.anchor: قال الحسين : ربنا إنك تعلم ما نخفي من الصحبة

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata reads the revealed Reminder as healing, mercy, clarification, and criterion that guides those destined for felicity and protects them from disobedience.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : نحن نزلنا الذكر شفاء

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: God preserves the Reminder in the hearts of His friends and employs the limbs of His elect servants in its service.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أي حفظه في قلوب أوليائه ويستعمل

rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: Ja'far says God's preservation accompanies those for whom He wills good through the span of life.
rows.anchor: وقال جعفر : ﴿ وإنا له لحافظون ﴾ على من أردنا به خيرا

words: فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُۥ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِى
rows.speaker: أبو عثمان
rows.claim: Abu Uthman says that after God distinguishes Adam through qualities of the spirit and repentance, the angels must stop disputing and submit to the command to prostrate.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : فإذا خصصته بإظهار النعت عليه من خصائص

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says Adam's knowledge, the spirit's knowledge, and its will are all constituted by God's knowing, knowledge, and willing; the spirit wills what God wills among its loves.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي : لما نفخ الروح في آدم جعل معرفتها معرفة الحق إياها

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The angels first saw Adam's form but not the spirit's divine attribution, repentance, knowledge of names, or glimpse of the unseen; when God disclosed these marks of special friendship and nearness, they prostrated.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : أبصرت الملائكة من آدم هيكله وشخصه

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti distinguishes Adam's spirit from other things by the completion of its form and the special divine attribution; it is brought near, enabled to know God's rule, effaced, and returned to God by indication.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي : الفرق بين روح آدم

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: The spirit is stripped of independent action and speech: it is adorned by God's creation, takes on His character, speaks through Him, and understands through His indication.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي : الفرق بين روح آدم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Obedient acts that come from people are transient, while God's recompense for those acts endures forever; the transient cannot equal what lasts.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : ما منكم من الطاعات فإنها فانية

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another says human obedience is flawed, whereas God's reward and recompense for it remain forever.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : طاعاتكم مدخولة وجزائي وثوابي على طاعاتكم

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata says human attributes perish while spiritual states endure; the servant must relinquish self-attributes and abide with God, since what comes from God remains.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أوصافكم فانية

rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: Ja'far identifies what people have as obligatory and supererogatory deeds, and what is with God as His attributes and qualities: originated things perish, while the pre-eternal remains.
rows.anchor: قال جعفر : ما عندكم ينفذ

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان
rows.claim: Abu Uthman says patience is rewarded by God's granting the servant contentment; one who truly follows the path of the patient receives the best reward in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : جزاء الصبر هو أن يعطي الله تعالى العبد رضا

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti derives the name Qur'an from its being conjoined with its speaker and not separate from Him, like sunlight and heat reaching us without separating from the sun's disk.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : سمي القرآن قرآنا لأنه مقارن

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata reads the verse as saying the Prophet should not suffer in God's service: his extra worship is gratitude for the nearness, communion, and service God granted him, and the gnostics find repose in such service.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : في قوله : ﴿ ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Ibn Ata cites the Prophet's reply to being asked why he worshipped so intensely after forgiveness: he asked whether he should not be a grateful servant.
rows.anchor: قال : ' أفلا أكون عبدا شكورا

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata addresses Muhammad as the leader of the fearful: the Quran was sent as a reminder for him to find repose and relief from fear, since a lover finds intimacy in the beloved's book and words.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : قيل له : يا محمد أنت إمام

rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: Ja'far says the Quran is admonition for the fearful, mercy for sinners, and intimacy for lovers.
rows.anchor: قال جعفر : أنزل الله القرآن موعظة للخائفين ورحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secret is an inspiration hidden from the servant's senses, reason, and awareness of angels and devils, lodged in the heart's core until will and decree bring it into manifestation and it moves through states.
rows.anchor: قال : السر ما يطالعه العبد ، ولا يطالعه الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is more hidden has not yet appeared and is known only to God; when its concealment is disclosed, its action begins.
rows.anchor: وما هو أخفى فما لم يحن ولم يطالع لا يعلمه إلا الله

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says the secret is what creatures do not know, and the more hidden is what God has not yet commanded to exist.
rows.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمه الله : السر ما خفي على العباد

rows.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
rows.claim: Al-Fudayl interprets God's knowledge of the secret and what is more hidden as knowledge of what is in a person's self and what that person will know tomorrow.
rows.anchor: سمعت الفضيل بن عياض يقول : في قوله : ﴿ يعلم السر

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd says God knows His secret within a person and the more hidden secret within that person.
rows.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله : يعلم سره فيك وأخفى سره

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti urges Moses to let no deed or word occupy his heart besides God, and to live in the beginningless and endless rather than in passing times and ages.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : لا يشغل قلبك بغيري فعلا

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata says the verse points to God's reality: references to beginning, end, times, and epochs are limitations that do not apply to Him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : إشارة إلى حقيقة الحق

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: God commands worship to make the creatures recognize their need and helplessness, not because He needs their service or is self-sufficient through it.
rows.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمه الله : أظهر هذا الخلق في شموخ

words: إِنَّنِىٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠
rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says God addressed Moses in Hebrew and described Himself to Muhammad in Arabic; the change of language does not change the divine attribute, just as commands and prohibitions vary without changing it.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا : بالعبرانية خاطب موسى ثم وصف لمحمد

rows.speaker: الحسين
rows.claim: Al-Husayn says the declaration removes every deity from human beings; once the inner secret is free of reverence for another, this declaration is no longer needed.
rows.anchor: قال الحسين : ﴿ لا إله إلا أنا ﴾ تنظيف البشر

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti sees the verse's sequence as beginning with unity of God and ending with the language of obedience in the command to establish prayer for His remembrance.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : ^ ( إنني إنا الله لا إله أنا فاعبدني ) ^ ابتدأه

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata reads establishing prayer for God's remembrance as remaining with Him in proper adab and not becoming heedless while turning toward Him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أقم معي بحسن الأدب

rows.speaker: فارس
rows.claim: Faris says Moses was nearly overwhelmed by speech unlike any he had heard; in that ecstatic state he claimed the staff as his own and answered beyond what was asked.
rows.anchor: قال فارس : سمع موسى كلاما لا يشبه كلام الحق

rows.speaker: فارس
rows.claim: When divine attributes overwhelmed Moses, God returned his attention to created things and occupied him with answering so he would not collapse under the sudden address.
rows.anchor: وقال : لما غلبت عليه الدعات الصفات رده الحق إلى المخلوق

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says the pleasure of direct address took Moses away from discernment, so he answered both the question asked and one not asked; the staff was a stick to him but a moving serpent in God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمه الله : استلذ الخطاب فأخذه عن التمييز

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: God alone knows the unseen realities of things; by asking Moses what was in his hand, God taught him that he knew only its appearance as a staff, while its reality and transformation were God's domain and display of power.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء في قوله : ﴿ وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى ﴾

rows.speaker: الحسين
rows.claim: Al-Husayn says God anchored Moses in his description of the staff and had him verify it; changing it into a serpent then exposed Moses' incapacity and provided a sign for the community.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسين : في قوله : ﴿ وما تلك بيمينك ﴾ قال : أثبته

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir says God made the question expansive to steady Moses' heart, knowing what would unfold when he witnessed divine majesty.
rows.anchor: وسمعت منصور بن عبد الله يقول : سمعت أبا بكر بن طاهر يقول

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir adds that God wanted Moses to speak at length so he would not feel constrained when asking.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا : أحب الله تعالى أن يبسط موسى في الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is told to cast away whatever his heart depends on or his soul settles into, since all such supports are veils and what one rests on will flee.
rows.anchor: فقال له : ألق كلما يعتمد عليه قلبك

rows.speaker: الحسين
rows.claim: Al-Husayn says Moses listed the staff's benefits while relying on it; casting it means removing from his heart love and reliance on its benefits, and taking it again means returning to God.
rows.anchor: قال الحسين : عدد موسى منافع العصا على ربه وسكونه إليها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation says the staff became a serpent during the address so it could serve as Moses' sign and miracle; without this prior witness, it would have frightened him in Pharaoh's presence.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن الحكمة في انقلاب العصا حية في وقت الكلام

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd says God alone knows hidden realities: Moses named the staff and its known uses, so God disclosed its hidden reality as a serpent beforehand, preventing panic and teaching him to turn back toward God without fear.
rows.anchor: سمعت منصور بن عبد الله يقول : سمعت جعفر بن نصير يقول سمعت الجنيد

rows.speaker: فارس
rows.claim: Faris says Moses listed the staff's uses so he could return to them in conversation and delight in his Master's address and reproach.
rows.anchor: قال فارس : ذكر كلما فيها من وجوه المنافع ليلا تكون له

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq says 'my staff' answers the question, while the following list of benefits gives thanks for God's gift of the staff.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق : قوله : ﴿ عصاي ﴾ جواب والذي بعده

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata says Moses' possessive wording wrongly claimed ownership before God; after the staff became a serpent he renounced that claim in fear, and God reassured him to take it without harm.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : في قوله : ﴿ عصاي ﴾ إضافة بالملك

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata says the staff held hidden secrets that Moses did not know, which God disclosed to him as signs and gifts of grace.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : سرائر مغيبة عني في العصا

rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: Ja'far says the greatest of the staff's many benefits was that it occasioned God's address: What is that in your right hand, Moses?
rows.anchor: قال جعفر : منافع شتى وأكبر منفعة لي فيها خطابك إياي

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl says God showed Moses uses he had not known: the staff became a serpent, struck the rock to release water, and struck the sea to split it, demonstrating that even prophets' knowledge of the worlds is limited beside God's.
rows.anchor: قال سهل : ذكر موسى من العصا مآرب ومنافع فأراه الله

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd says Moses' fear was fear of being overpowered by divine might, not an instinctive or natural fear.
rows.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله : كان خوف موسى عليه السلام خوف تسليط

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says Moses saw on the staff a sign or covering of God's displeasure and punishment, so he did not feel safe from divine hidden power.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : خوف موسى من العصا أنه شاهد أثر

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: After speaking with God, Moses sees no merit in speaking with anyone else; when sent to Pharaoh he asks God to free his tongue so he can address a creature after hearing God's address.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : لما كلم الله موسى عليه السلام لم يكن بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata asks to see none but God, act and speak only through knowledge of Him, and loosen the human knot of the tongue so that Moses speaks only what he has received from God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : اكشف لي عن صدري حتى لا أشاهد غيرك

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata identifies the knot in Moses' tongue as the knot of the lower self.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا : أراد به العقدة النفسانية

rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: Ja'far says God's address had tied Moses' tongue against speaking to others; when sent to Pharaoh, Moses asks for release so he can fulfill the command completely.
rows.anchor: قال جعفر : لما كلم الله موسى عقد لسانه موسى عن مكالمة

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata asks God to uncover his heart so he sees none but Him, free him from self-regard, and make him speak only of God's favor and what brings him near.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : اشرح لي صدري ' اكشف لي قلبي

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن عبد الله بن طاهر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Abd Allah ibn Tahir says Moses' breast constricted at addressing people after standing with God, so he asked for ease in speaking to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: سمعت أبا بكر بن عبد الله بن طاهر يقول : ضاق صدر موسى

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata reads the requests as opening the breast to hear God, easing the affair through abiding with Him, and loosening the ego's knot from the tongue.
rows.anchor: سمعت منصور بن عبد الله يقول : سمعت أبا القاسم البزار يقول : قال ابن عطاء

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd says Moses asked God only for good character traits.
rows.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله في قوله

rows.speaker: الحسين
rows.claim: Al-Husayn reads the requests as progression into direct encounter: expanded capacity for confrontation, an eased course to God by God, and a loosened tongue; once granted, Moses sees only God's part in him and receives all he asked.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسين : لما أزال الحق عنه التوقف وجاء إلى الله بالله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Moses asked to have the knot of shyness removed because he was embarrassed to address God's enemy Pharaoh with the tongue that had addressed God.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : سأله حل عقدة الحياء عنه فإنه استحيى

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl warns against abundant verbal remembrance that leaves the heart inattentive and unwatchful.
rows.anchor: قال سهل : لا تكثر الذكر باللسان

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Mu'adh says it is right to love the world: it is humanity's mother and place of growth and provision, the place of return, and the righteous' road to God and His nearness.
rows.anchor: - قيل ليحيى بن معاذ : ما بال الإنسان يحب الدنيا

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata says Moses need not fear because God sees and hears him and is with him; Moses relies on the Causer while his opponents depend on material causes.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ' لا تخف فإنك بمرأى منا

words: لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ
rows.speaker: ذو النون
rows.claim: Dhu al-Nun says whoever prefers God to everything finds sacrifice in God's cause easy, having chosen what is precious and taken on a light burden.
rows.anchor: قال ذو النون : من آثر الله على الأشياء هان عليه

words: لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians' declaration shows that what God disclosed to them made carrying burdens and meeting harm easy, because the vision they received was easy to bear.
rows.anchor: قال الله : جاء كيسا على السحرة لن نؤثرك

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the request means: make me knowledgeable of You and ignorant of everything besides You; that is true increase in knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : اجعلني عالما بك

rows.speaker: محمد بن الفضل
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl reads the request as increased knowledge of one's own hidden evils, schemes, and excuses, so one can treat them with God's help.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن الفضل : ﴿ رب زدني علما ﴾ بنفسي

words: وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ مِن قَبْلُ
rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata says Adam was charged to obey no one besides God; he forgot the covenant by looking to the garden with his eye rather than attending to God with his inner secret.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء في قوله : ﴿ ولقد عهدنا إلى آدم ﴾ قال : عهدنا إلى آدم

rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: Ja'far says Adam was charged not to forget God in any state, but the garden's delight distracted him from its giver; expulsion taught him that true bliss is nearness to God, not food and drink.
rows.anchor: قال جعفر : عهدنا إلى آدم أن لا ينسانا في حال ونسينا

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata says Adam lacked resolve because, on entering the garden, he attended to his own deed rather than God's grace.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ﴿ لم نجد له عزما ﴾ لم يطالع في دخول

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti explains the lack of resolve as inability to restrain himself; God concealed Adam from witnessing himself so he could see signs of servitude as admonition and adornment.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : ﴿ فنسي ولم نجد له عزما ﴾ أي قوة

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says 'he forgot' has two senses, distinguishing one who forgets in God's presence from one who forgets in absence.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : ' فنسي ' له وجهان

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti supports the distinction with the Prophet's report that error and forgetfulness are lifted from his community.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' رفع عن أمتي الخطأ والنسيان '

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another says Adam forgot God's command at the moment he partook of the fruit.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : نسي في وقت التناول مطالعة الأمر

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم النصرآباذي
rows.claim: Al-Nasrabadi distinguishes a sin that obliges one to seek forgiveness from a sin one is made to commit and is excused for.
rows.anchor: سمعت أبا القاسم النصرآباذي يقول : ذنب لزمته فوجب عليك

rows.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
rows.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl interprets Adam's lack of resolve as returning to the sin a second time.
rows.anchor: قال الحسين بن الفضل في قوله : ﴿ ولم نجد له عزما ﴾

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says Adam concealed his enemy's hostility and did not implore God for protection, so he listened to the enemy's speech and oath.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : أضمر عداوته

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata explains the singular 'you will suffer' rather than dual 'you two will suffer': Adam knew the special rank of direct address while Eve did not, so he is named as the principal and she follows him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء في هذه الآية : ﴿ فلا يخرجنكما من الجنة فتشقى ﴾
